title: This Giant Salamander Breathes Through Its Wrinkles
subject: hellbender salamander

scenes.text: This giant salamander breathes through its wrinkles.
It's the biggest salamander in North America, up to 29 inches long.
It has lungs. It barely relies on them.
Loose folds of skin run along its sides, packed with tiny blood vessels that pull oxygen straight from the water.
That's why it needs cool, clear streams. Dirty, warm water means less air.
The wrinkles aren't a flaw. They're how it breathes.

description:
This giant salamander breathes through its wrinkles.
The hellbender has lungs, but most of its oxygen comes through folds of skin along its sides.
Have you ever seen one in the wild?
first_comment: Would you ever have guessed those wrinkles were its lungs? What weird body part should we cover next?
